claims.statement: There is an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every p, zero or prime, there is m₀ with the following property. Over every field of characteristic p and for every m ≥ m₀, every circuit for HCₘ, and every circuit for PERMₘ if p ≠ 2, has more than m^(c (log m)^(1/3)) gates. (Here log = log₂.)

claims.reference: Theorem 1.4, first sentence (proved as Theorem N.5)
claims.statement: Theorem 1.1 holds for circuits that approximate HCₘ, respectively PERMₘ.
Over every field, VP is a proper subset of VNP.

claims.reference: Theorem 1.4, second sentence (proved as Theorem N.5)
claims.statement: In particular VNP ⊄ VP̄ (the closure of VP) over every field.
There are c > 0 and m₀ such that for all m ≥ m₀ every circuit over ℝ that computes PERMₘ has more than m^(c (log m)^(1/3)) = 2^(c (log m)^(4/3)) gates.
